title: Procurement-to-Cash Controls and Forecast Reconciliation Runbook
author: Miguel Torres
content:
Overview

This runbook defines the controls and operational procedures that connect procurement events, contractual milestones, billing triggers, and revenue recognition forecasts for Redwood Inference. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and revenue operations stakeholders who manage: vendor and customer contracts, invoice routing, forecasting inputs, and recurring billing pipelines.

Scope

- Applies to all customer contracts, procurement commitments, and vendor invoices that have direct or indirect impact on revenue recognition, cash collection, or the revenue forecast (ARR, MRR, and deferred revenue balances).
- Covers the end-to-end procurement-to-cash (P2C) path for both Hosted API and Dedicated/Private contract types.
- Excludes payroll and taxes (handled by People Ops and Tax).

Goals and success metrics

- Ensure >99% accuracy between contract terms and billing triggers prior to invoice issuance.
- Reduce forecast adjustment churn to <1% of ARR per month attributable to contract mis-mapping.
- Maintain an audit trail linking each revenue recognition entry to a contract clause and an executed procurement event.

Ownership and primary contacts

- Finance (Revenue Ops) — primary owner for forecast reconciliations, revrec entries, and reporting. (Contact: Miguel Torres)
- Legal — owner of contract clause interpretation and amendment approvals. (Contact: Elena Karpova)
- Procurement — owner of vendor commitments, PO issuance, and supplier controls. (Contact: Aisha Patel)
- Billing/Payments — owner of invoice generation, payment capture, and disputes. (Contact: Ravi Menon)

Key controls (high level)

1) Contract-to-billing mapping: every executed contract must include a billing trigger table (see template in Appendix) and a unique Contract ID (CID) that surfaces in the billing system.
2) Purchase Order (PO) linkage: supplier and customer POs must be linked to the CID or internal commit ID before processing.
3) Approval gates: revenue-impacting discounts, credits, or credit notes require delegated approval documented in the contract system.
4) Forecast feed locking: once a monthly forecast window is closed, upstream contract changes that affect closed months must post an adjustment memo and be flagged for FP&A review.
5) Audit trail: all revrec entries must reference a source: CID, invoice ID, and journal entry.

Procedure: Contract ingestion and initial mapping (step-by-step)

1. Contract executed (Legal stamps signed copy) -> Legal uploads signed contract to Contract Repository and assigns CID.
2. Legal populates the Contract Metadata form (contract type, start/end dates, billing cadence, termination/renewal clauses, standard revrec code) and flags any non-standard terms.
3. Revenue Ops receives CID and performs a contract mapping review within 3 business days: confirm billing cadence, milestone vs. usage billing, and discount schedules.
4. If contract is non-standard, Revenue Ops runs a RevRec impact assessment and produces an implementation checklist. Legal/Revenue Ops agree on billing trigger mapping before the contract is activated in the Billing system.

Billing trigger mapping table (required content in contract metadata)

| Procurement/Contract Event | Billing Trigger Type | Billing System Field | RevRec Recognition Policy |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Annual prepay (customer pays upfront) | Upfront invoice | invoice.type = "prepay"; invoice.schedule = "single" | Recognize ratably over service term (ASC 606: performance obligations) |
| Monthly metered usage | Usage invoice | invoice.metric = "tokens"; invoice.period = yyyy-mm | Recognize as invoiced (when performance obligation satisfied) |
| Dedicated reserved capacity (commit) | Periodic recurring invoice | invoice.type = "subscription"; invoice.terms.cadence = "monthly" | Recognize monthly as service delivered |
| One-time professional services | Milestone invoice | invoice.type = "milestone"; invoice.milestone_id = MID | Recognize on completion of milestone or per acceptance criteria |

Note: Contracts with mixed billing (prepay + usage) must list both rows and include a primary CID-level mapping.

Forecast reconciliation cadence and runbook

Weekly cadence (operational):
- Owners: Revenue Ops + Sales Ops
- Inputs: latest closed invoices, adjustments (credit notes), newly executed contracts (CID additions), churned accounts, payment failures flagged by Billing.
- Outputs: delta report for FP&A, flagged exceptions (contracts with missing billing triggers), and updated MRR/ARR metrics in the Forecasting dashboard.

Monthly cadence (financial close):
- Pre-close checkpoint (T-5 business days): Revenue Ops publishes the contract change log for the month and any expected adjustments.
- Close window (T-2 to T+3 days): FP&A ingests revised inputs and posts final month-end revenue recognition journal entries.
- Post-close review (T+10): Finance runs a reconciliation: deferred revenue opening balance + billings - recognized revenue = deferred revenue closing balance. Discrepancies >0.5% require a root-cause memo.

Runbook: Weekly forecast reconciliation (detailed)

1. Pull datasets:
   - SQL: SELECT cid, start_date, end_date, billing_cadence, price_day, amount FROM contracts WHERE state = 'active';
   - Invoices API: /v1/invoices?status=posted&period=YYYY-MM
   - Billing adjustments: export credit_notes.csv from Billing portal.
2. Join by CID, aggregate billings by period, compare to forecast bucket for same period.
3. Flag items where abs(billing - forecast) > $5,000 OR >5% of forecast bucket.
4. Investigate flagged items: common root causes include unlinked PO/CID, unprocessed amendment, or manual credit memo.
5. Resolution: document fix in the exception tracker and update forecast for next weekly run.

Billing and revenue recognition escalation matrix

- Level 1 (Billing ops): invoice formatting, payment posting, charge sequencing. SLA: 1 business day.
- Level 2 (Revenue Ops): revrec policy questions, mapping disputes, reclassification requests. SLA: 3 business days.
- Level 3 (Legal / FP&A): contract interpretation, significant policy exceptions (> $50k impact) or audit escalations. SLA: 5 business days.

Controls for procurement spend that impacts revenue forecasts

- Commit-to-PO principle: Any procurement commitment over $50k that would materially affect unit economics or forecasted cost of goods sold must be routed through Finance and documented with an impact memo.
- Vendor refunds/credits: Credit memos issued by suppliers that affect recognized revenue or cost allocations must be approved by Procurement and Finance before posting.
- Capital vs. expense gating: Onboarding expenses (e.g., on-prem packaging with >12 month life) must be filtered through the capitalization workflow. See Appendix B for the capitalization decision checklist.

Audit and evidence requirements

Each monthly revrec posting must include links to: signed contract (CID), invoice(s), payment confirmation (if cash basis), and a short audit justification note. Standard evidence folder naming convention: /evidence/revrec/YYYY/MM/CID-<cid>.zip

Common exceptions and how to resolve them

- Missing CID on invoice: Attach signed contract to invoice in Billing and re-run invoice validation.
- Discount applied but not approved: Open a variance ticket and reverse invoice; require Sales and Finance approval for reissue.
- Duplicate invoice: Flag in Billing system and create a credit memo referencing original invoice ID.

Appendix A — Contract metadata template (fields required)

- CID (string)
- Customer name (string)
- Contract type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Start date / End date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Billing cadence (monthly / quarterly / annually / usage)
- Billing triggers (description + mapping table)
- RevRec policy (text reference to internal policy code)
- Owner (Sales owner, Revenue Ops owner)

Appendix B — Capitalization decision checklist

1. Is the asset expected to provide economic benefit > 12 months? (Y/N)
2. Is the total cost > $5,000? (Y/N)
3. Is the asset a component of an installable on-prem package delivered to a customer? (Y/N)
4. If two or more answers are Yes, route to Capitalization committee for approval.

Appendix C — Example remediation SQL (use with care)

-- Find invoices with no CID linked
SELECT invoice_id, customer_id, total_amount FROM invoices WHERE cid IS NULL AND status = 'posted' LIMIT 100;

-- Aggregate billed vs forecast by month
SELECT date_trunc('month', invoice_date) AS month, SUM(total_amount) as billed, f.forecast_value
FROM invoices i
JOIN forecasts f ON date_trunc('month', i.invoice_date) = f.month
GROUP BY 1, f.forecast_value
ORDER BY month DESC;

Operational notes and tooling

- The Forecasting dashboard is the single source of truth for MRR and ARR; Revenue Ops is responsible for publishing the weekly snapshot every Monday by 09:00 PT.
- Use the Exception Tracker (Spreadsheet link stored in Team Drive) to drive investigations. Each exception must have a documented owner and resolution ETA.
- Critical escalations should be opened in the Finance Slack channel #finance-ops-escalations and must include CID, invoice id, and a 1-paragraph summary.
